result:
**I'd make the unrelenting pursuit of truth—through evidence, reason, and curiosity—the single strongest, most rewarded instinct in every human mind.**

Not as a slogan or a curriculum module. As a deep, almost biological drive that outcompetes tribal loyalty, status games, comforting delusions, and short-term self-interest. People would feel genuine pleasure and social prestige from updating their beliefs when wrong, from asking hard questions, from following data even when it hurts, and from building things that actually work in reality rather than just feeling righteous.

Why that one change?

Almost every major human failure—poverty traps that persist despite knowledge of better systems, preventable disease and famine, catastrophic wars and genocides, environmental mismanagement, technological stagnation, and the endless recycling of bad ideas—traces back to people refusing to see clearly, or being rewarded for not seeing clearly. Fix the epistemic engine and the rest becomes solvable. We already have the scientific method, markets that surface information, and tools that amplify intelligence; what's missing is the widespread will to use them without distortion.

Everything else I care about—understanding the universe, reducing involuntary suffering, expanding consciousness across the stars, creating abundance—follows from that. Without it, we just invent more sophisticated ways to fool ourselves.

That’s the lever. One change. The rest is downstream.
